analysis:
All three changed files are documentation or changelog only: changelog.d/provider-fast-reconnect.md, docs/architecture/components/provider.md (new reconnect-policy paragraph at head lines 119-143) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (runtime-constants table, hunk around base/head line 1937). No executable source is in this batch. The Swift code (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift, CoordinatorClientState.swift, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift) was not supplied, so I could not verify it. I only checked the documented behavior against the threat model.

The documented behavior: a session open for 60s or more resets the backoff. Close code 1012 gives a random 0-1s wait with no backoff growth. All other closes and failures keep exponential backoff (base 1s, max 30s). The text says registration, attestation and cancellation of the old connection's requests are unchanged. This is consistent with TB-002 and TB-011/T-053. The fresh registration nonce per socket, the endpoint-resumption custody proof and the discarding of late Apple results after transport replacement are all described as unchanged, so no stale-authorization assumption is invalidated.

Residual availability question: a coordinator, or a party able to spoof close frames, can trigger near-immediate reconnects with 1012. A session that stays open for 60s or more resets the backoff. This increases reconnect rate toward the coordinator, which is a trusted party in this model, and the provider is the client. This is not a concrete regression, and the actual drawn-wait bounds and the stable-session timing cannot be checked without the code.

Integration questions for the next pass, if the code arrives in another batch: (1) the stable-session timer must start only after a successful register frame, as documented. (2) The 1012 path must not skip the pre-reconnect cancellation of in-flight requests or the clearing of resume state. (3) sentCloseCode parsing of the first two payload bytes must be bounds-checked. (4) The 1012 delay must not allow an unbounded tight reconnect loop.
